    32→

    35→```

   127→      ├── manifest.json        # Compact metadata for fast listing
   128→      ├── intent.md            # Human-readable reasoning summary
   129→      ├── transcript.jsonl     # Full session, one message per line

# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

## Project Overview

Engram captures AI agent reasoning as first-class, versioned data in Git. Each "engram" is a discrete unit of reasoning memory (intent, transcript, tool calls, rejected approaches, token economics) linked to the Git commits it produced. Engrams are stored as native Git objects under `.git/refs/engrams/` — no sidecar database.

## Current State

This is a **greenfield project**. The repository contains only a design document (`readme`). Implementation has not started. The planned language is **Rust** with Python and TypeScript SDKs.

## Planned Architecture

```
engram-cli          CLI binary (user interface)
engram-core         Data model, Git storage engine, hooks, config
engram-capture      Session capture (wrapper, import, HTTP server)
engram-query        Search index (Tantivy), context graph, analytics
engram-protocol     Wire format for agent ↔ server communication
engram-sdk          Rust SDK for direct agent integration
sdks/python/        Python SDK
sdks/typescript/    TypeScript SDK
```

This is a Cargo workspace. Each `engram-*` crate is a separate member.

## Key Design Decisions

- **Git-native storage**: Engrams are Git tree objects stored under `.git/refs/engrams/<ab>/<full-hash>`, containing `manifest.json`, `intent.md`, `transcript.jsonl`, `operations.json`, and `lineage.json`.
- **Commit trailers**: Commits get `Engram-Id`, `Engram-Agent`, `Engram-Tokens`, `Engram-Cost` trailers for discoverability.
- **Three capture modes**: Wrapper (PTY spawn of any agent), session import (parse known agent formats), SDK integration (direct API).
- **Tantivy** for full-text search indexing of reasoning content.
- **Context graph**: Engrams, files, functions, agents, and concepts as nodes; edges are "modified by", "motivated by", "depends on", "rejected in favor of".

## Build Commands (once implemented)

```bash
cargo build                       # Build all crates
cargo test                        # Run all tests
cargo test -p engram-core         # Test a single crate
cargo run -p engram-cli -- <cmd>  # Run the CLI
cargo install --path engram-cli   # Install locally
```

## License

Apache-2.0 OR MIT (dual-licensed).

# Engram: Full Implementation Plan

## Context

Engram is a greenfield Rust project that captures AI agent reasoning (intent, transcripts, tool calls, dead ends, token economics) as native Git objects. The repository currently contains only a design document (`readme`). This plan covers the full build from empty repo to production-ready application across 7 phases.

---

## Phase 1: Foundation (engram-core + engram-cli skeleton)

### 1.1 Cargo Workspace Setup

Create a virtual workspace at the root with two initial crates:

**`/Cargo.toml`** — Virtual manifest:
- `resolver = "2"`, `edition = "2024"`, `rust-version = "1.85"`
- Members: `crates/engram-core`, `crates/engram-cli`
- `[workspace.dependencies]`: git2 0.20, serde 1 (derive), serde_json 1, chrono 0.4 (serde), uuid 1 (v4, serde), thiserror 2, anyhow 1, clap 4.5 (derive, env), tracing 0.1, tracing-subscriber 0.3 (env-filter), tempfile 3, assert_cmd 2, predicates 3

**`crates/engram-core/Cargo.toml`** — Library crate with git2, serde, serde_json, chrono, uuid, thiserror, tracing. Dev-dep: tempfile.

**`crates/engram-cli/Cargo.toml`** — Binary crate (`[[bin]] name = "engram"`), depends on engram-core, clap, anyhow, tracing, tracing-subscriber. Dev-deps: assert_cmd, predicates, tempfile.

Also create: `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (fmt check, clippy, test on ubuntu/macos/windows, build release), `.gitignore`, `LICENSE-MIT`, `LICENSE-APACHE`.

### 1.2 Data Model (`crates/engram-core/src/model/`)

**`engram.rs`** — `EngramId` (newtype around String, UUID v4 hex no dashes), `Manifest` (id, version:u32, created_at, finished_at, agent:AgentInfo, git_commits:Vec<String>, token_usage:TokenUsage, summary:Option<String>, tags:Vec<String>, capture_mode:CaptureMode), `AgentInfo` (name, model:Option, version:Option), `CaptureMode` enum (Wrapper, Import, Sdk). `EngramId::fanout_prefix()` returns first 2 chars.

**`token_economics.rs`** — `TokenUsage` (input_tokens:u64, output_tokens:u64, cache_read_tokens:u64, cache_write_tokens:u64, total_tokens:u64, cost_usd:Option<f64>). Default impl.

**`intent.rs`** — `Intent` (original_request:String, interpreted_goal:Option, summary:Option, dead_ends:Vec<DeadEnd>, decisions:Vec<Decision>), `DeadEnd` (approach, reason), `Decision` (description, rationale). Methods: `to_markdown() -> String`, `from_markdown(&str) -> Result`. Markdown format: `# Intent` / `## Summary` / `## Dead Ends` / `## Decisions` sections.

**`transcript.rs`** — `TranscriptEntry` (timestamp, role:Role, content:TranscriptContent, token_count:Option<u64>), `Role` enum (User, Assistant, System, Tool), `TranscriptContent` internally-tagged enum (Text{text}, ToolUse{tool_name, tool_id, input:Value}, ToolResult{tool_id, output, is_error}, Thinking{text}), `Transcript` (entries:Vec). Methods: `to_jsonl() -> Vec<u8>`, `from_jsonl(&[u8]) -> Result`.

**`operations.rs`** — `Operations` (tool_calls:Vec<ToolCall>, file_changes:Vec<FileChange>, shell_commands:Vec<ShellCommand>), `ToolCall` (timestamp, tool_name, input:Value, output_summary:Option, duration_ms:Option, is_error), `FileChange` (path, change_type:FileChangeType, lines_added:Option, lines_removed:Option), `FileChangeType` enum (Created, Modified, Deleted, Renamed{from}), `ShellCommand` (timestamp, command, exit_code:Option, duration_ms:Option).

**`lineage.rs`** — `Lineage` (parent_engram:Option<EngramId>, child_engrams:Vec, related_engrams:Vec<Relationship>, git_commits:Vec<String>, branch:Option<String>), `Relationship` (engram_id, relation_type:RelationType, description:Option), `RelationType` enum (FollowsFrom, Motivates, DependsOn, Supersedes, ConflictsWith).

**`mod.rs`** — Re-export all public types.

**`EngramData`** aggregate struct (manifest, intent, transcript, operations, lineage) — used for create/read operations.

### 1.3 Git Storage Engine (`crates/engram-core/src/storage/`)

**`objects.rs`** — `create_engram_objects(repo: &Repository, data: &EngramData) -> Result<Oid>`:
1. Serialize each component to bytes (manifest→JSON, intent→Markdown, transcript→JSONL, operations→JSON, lineage→JSON)
2. Create 5 blobs via `repo.blob(&bytes)`
3. Build tree via `repo.treebuilder(None)` → `insert("manifest.json", oid, 0o100644)` for each → `write()`
4. Create commit via `repo.commit(None, &sig, &sig, &message, &tree, &[])` — standalone, no parent
5. Return commit Oid

**`refs.rs`** — Constants: `ENGRAM_REF_PREFIX = "refs/engrams/"`. Functions: `engram_ref_name(id) -> String` (format `refs/engrams/{prefix}/{full}`), `create_engram_ref(repo, id, oid)`, `delete_engram_ref(repo, id)`, `list_engram_refs(repo) -> Vec<(EngramId, Oid)>` (glob `refs/engrams/*/*`).

**`read.rs`** — `read_engram(repo, commit_oid) -> Result<EngramData>` (commit→tree→blobs, deserialize each), `read_manifest(repo, commit_oid) -> Result<Manifest>` (fast path, reads only manifest.json blob). Helpers: `read_blob_bytes`, `read_blob_string`, `read_blob_json<T>`.

**`git_backend.rs`** — `GitStorage` struct wrapping `git2::Repository`. Methods:
- `open(path)`, `discover()` — open/find repo
- `is_initialized() -> bool` — check `engram.enabled` config
- `init()` — set config values, add refspecs to remotes
- `create(data: &EngramData) -> Result<EngramId>` — call objects::create + refs::create
- `read(id) -> Result<EngramData>`, `read_manifest(id) -> Result<Manifest>`
- `list(opts: &ListOptions) -> Result<Vec<Manifest>>` — iterate refs, read manifests
- `delete(id)` — remove ref
- `repo()`, `workdir()` — accessors

### 1.4 Config (`crates/engram-core/src/config/`)

**`settings.rs`** — `EngramConfig` (enabled:bool, auto_capture:bool, default_agent:Option, push_on_push:bool, index_path:Option). Stored in `.git/config` under `[engram]`. Methods: `load(config)`, `save(config)`, `default_init()`.

### 1.5 Error Types (`crates/engram-core/src/error.rs`)

`CoreError` enum with thiserror: Git(git2::Error), NotFound{id}, InvalidManifest(serde_json::Error), NotInitialized, Config(String), Io(io::Error), Utf8(FromUtf8Error), MissingBlob(String).

### 1.6 CLI (`crates/engram-cli/src/`)

**`main.rs`** — Cli struct with clap Parser: `-v` verbosity (count), `--format` (text/json), subcommand. Init tracing subscriber with env filter. Dispatch to command handlers.

**`commands/mod.rs`** — Commands enum: Init, Log, Show, Version.

**`commands/init.rs`** — InitArgs (--force). Opens repo, calls storage.init(), prints next steps.

**`commands/log.rs`** — LogArgs (--cost, -n/--limit, --agent). Lists manifests, formats as table or JSON. Shows: short-id, summary, agent, timestamp, optionally cost/tokens.

**`commands/show.rs`** — ShowArgs (id:String, --intent, --transcript, --operations). Resolves "HEAD" to most recent engram. Displays full engram or requested section.

**`commands/version.rs`** — Prints version from Cargo.toml.

**`output/mod.rs`** — OutputFormat enum (Text, Json). **`output/format.rs`** — Formatting functions for manifests and engram data.

### 1.7 Testing

- **Unit tests**: Serialization roundtrips for all model types. EngramId generation and fanout. Intent markdown roundtrip. Transcript JSONL roundtrip.
- **Storage integration tests** (`crates/engram-core/tests/`): Create temp repo via `git2::Repository::init(tempdir)`, create engram, list, read back, verify all fields, delete, verify gone.
- **CLI integration tests** (`crates/engram-cli/tests/`): `assert_cmd` tests for `engram version`, `engram init` in temp repo, `engram log` (empty).

### 1.8 Done When

- `cargo build --workspace` succeeds with no warnings
- `cargo test --workspace` passes
- `cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings` clean
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` passes
- Full create → list → read → delete lifecycle works

---

## Phase 2: Capture (engram-capture)

**Depends on**: Phase 1

### 2.1 Setup

Add `engram-capture` to workspace. New deps: portable-pty 0.9, vt100 0.15, tokio 1 (full), sha2 0.10.

### 2.2 PTY Wrapper (`crates/engram-capture/src/pty/`)

**`wrapper.rs`** — `PtyWrapperConfig` (command, args, working_dir, agent_name, rows, cols). `PtySession` struct. `PtySession::start(config) -> Result<Self>` snapshots working tree, spawns command in PTY. `PtySession::run(self) -> Result<CapturedSession>` runs to completion, detects file changes.

**`stream.rs`** — `PtyStream` handles bidirectional I/O: stdin→master_writer, master_reader→stdout+capture_buffer. Uses vt100::Parser for ANSI stripping. Runs on threads (not async, because portable-pty I/O is blocking).

**`detector.rs`** — `snapshot_working_tree(root) -> HashMap<PathBuf, Vec<u8>>` (path→SHA256, ignores .git, respects .gitignore). `detect_changes(before, after) -> Vec<FileChange>`.

**`CapturedSession`** struct: raw_output, parsed_screen (cleaned text), start/end time, exit_code, file_changes, command, args.

### 2.3 Session Finalization (`crates/engram-capture/src/session/`)

**`builder.rs`** — `SessionBuilder` takes AgentInfo + CapturedSession, produces EngramData. `build_and_store(storage) -> Result<EngramId>`.

**`summarizer.rs`** — `extract_intent_from_pty(captured) -> Intent` (first arg/line = original_request, file changes = summary). `extract_operations_from_pty(captured) -> Operations` (best-effort for PTY mode).

### 2.4 Git Hooks (`crates/engram-core/src/hooks/`)

**`installer.rs`** — `install_hooks(repo)` writes shell scripts to `.git/hooks/` that invoke `engram hook-handler <hook-name>`. Chains with existing hooks.

**`post_commit.rs`** — Reads `.git/engram-session` (ActiveSession JSON), appends HEAD commit SHA to commits list.

**`prepare_commit_msg.rs`** — Reads active session, appends Engram-Id/Agent/Tokens/Cost trailers to commit message.

**ActiveSession** (stored at `.git/engram-session`): engram_id, agent, started_at, commits:Vec<String>. Created when recording starts, deleted when recording ends.

### 2.5 CLI

Add `Record` command: `engram record -- <command> [args...]`. TrailingVarArg for command. `--agent` override. Lifecycle: create session file → snapshot → spawn PTY → run → detect changes → build engram → store → cleanup → print summary.

### 2.6 Done When

- `engram record -- echo "hello"` captures output and stores engram
- PTY stdin/stdout pass-through works transparently
- File change detection identifies created/modified/deleted files
- Hooks install correctly, trailers added to commits during recording
- `engram log` and `engram show` work with captured engrams

---

## Phase 3: Import (part of engram-capture)

**Depends on**: Phase 1 (Phase 2's session builder is reused but could be factored out)

### 3.1 Claude Code Importer (`crates/engram-capture/src/import/claude_code.rs`)

Parses `~/.claude/projects/<path-encoded>/<sessionId>.jsonl`. Internal types: `ClaudeCodeEntry` (type, parentUuid, uuid, sessionId, message, timestamp), `ClaudeMessage` (role, content:Value, model, usage). Logic:
1. Read JSONL line by line, parse as ClaudeCodeEntry
2. Filter to type "user"/"assistant" (skip "progress", "file-history-snapshot")
3. Build linked list via parentUuid→uuid chains
4. Convert content blocks (text, tool_use, tool_result, thinking) → TranscriptEntry
5. Accumulate TokenUsage from usage fields
6. First user message → Intent.original_request
7. Tool calls → Operations
8. Path encoding: `/Users/sjonas/project` → `-Users-sjonas-project`

Public API: `ClaudeCodeImporter::import_session(path) -> Result<EngramData>`, `discover_sessions(project_path) -> Vec<PathBuf>`, `projects_dir() -> Option<PathBuf>`.

### 3.2 Aider Importer (`crates/engram-capture/src/import/aider.rs`)

Parses `.aider.chat.history.md`. Format: `#### ` = user message, following text = assistant, `> ` = tool output, `Tokens:` lines for costs. Split on `#### ` boundaries, group exchanges into sessions.

### 3.3 Auto-Detection (`crates/engram-capture/src/import/detect.rs`)

`ImportSource` enum (ClaudeCode{path}, Aider{path}). `detect_sources(repo_root) -> Vec<ImportSource>` checks for Claude Code project dir and .aider.chat.history.md.

### 3.4 CLI

Add `Import` command: `engram import [path] --format <fmt> --auto-detect --dry-run`.

### 3.5 Test Fixtures

Create `crates/engram-capture/tests/fixtures/` with sample Claude Code JSONL and Aider markdown files.

### 3.6 Done When

- `engram import <path> --format claude-code` imports correctly
- `engram import --auto-detect` discovers sessions
- Token usage accumulated, tool calls extracted, intent populated

---

## Phase 4: Query & Search (engram-query)

**Depends on**: Phase 1

### 4.1 Setup

Add `engram-query` to workspace. New dep: tantivy 0.25.

### 4.2 Tantivy Schema (`crates/engram-query/src/index/schema.rs`)

`EngramSchema` struct with field handles: id (STRING|STORED), intent_request (TEXT|STORED), intent_summary (TEXT|STORED), transcript_text (TEXT), agent_name (STRING|STORED), agent_model (STRING|STORED), created_at (date INDEXED|STORED), file_paths (TEXT|STORED), dead_ends (TEXT|STORED), cost_usd (f64 INDEXED|STORED), total_tokens (u64 INDEXED|STORED), manifest_json (STORED only).

### 4.3 Writer/Reader

**`index/writer.rs`** — `EngramIndexWriter::open(path)`, `index_engram(data)` (concatenates transcript text entries, dead ends text, file paths into searchable fields), `commit()`, `delete_engram(id)`.

**`index/reader.rs`** — `EngramSearcher::open(path)`, `search(query, limit) -> Vec<SearchResult>` (parses query against intent_request, intent_summary, transcript_text, dead_ends, file_paths fields), `search_by_file(path, limit)`.

**`index/rebuild.rs`** — `rebuild_index(storage, index_path) -> Result<usize>` — deletes and recreates index from all Git engrams.

### 4.4 High-Level APIs

**`search.rs`** — `SearchEngine::open(storage)` (resolves `.git/engram-index/`), delegates to reader.

**`trace.rs`** — `trace_file(storage, search, file_path) -> Vec<TraceEntry>` — all engrams that touched a file.

**`diff.rs`** — `diff_engrams(storage, id_a, id_b) -> EngramDiff` — common files, unique files, token/cost deltas.

### 4.5 CLI

Add commands: `Search` (query, -n/--limit), `Trace` (file path), `Diff` (id_a, id_b), `Reindex`.

Index auto-updates: `GitStorage::create()` checks for `.git/engram-index/` existence and indexes the new engram if present. First `engram search` creates the index if missing.

### 4.6 Done When

- `engram search "auth"` returns relevant results with BM25 ranking
- `engram trace src/auth.rs` shows reasoning history
- `engram reindex` rebuilds from scratch
- Index at `.git/engram-index/` (inside .git, auto-excluded)

---

## Phase 5: Protocol & Sync (engram-protocol)

**Depends on**: Phase 1

### 5.1 Setup

Add `engram-protocol` to workspace. Deps: engram-core, git2, thiserror, tracing.

### 5.2 Implementation

**`refspec.rs`** — Constants: ENGRAM_FETCH_REFSPEC (`+refs/engrams/*:refs/engrams/*`), ENGRAM_PUSH_REFSPEC. `ensure_refspecs(repo, remote_name)` adds if missing.

**`sync.rs`** — `push_engrams(repo, remote, opts) -> PushResult`, `fetch_engrams(repo, remote, opts) -> FetchResult`. Uses `git2::Remote::push/fetch` with engram refspecs. PushOptions: specific_ids, dry_run. FetchOptions: specific_ids, metadata_only.

**`selective.rs`** — Thin engrams (manifest+lineage only) under `refs/engrams-meta/`. `is_full_engram()`, `fetch_full_engram()`.

### 5.3 CLI

Add commands: `Push` (remote, default origin), `Pull` (fetch + reindex), `Fetch` (remote).

### 5.4 Done When

- Push/fetch work between local repos (test with bare repo as remote)
- `engram init` configures refspecs on existing remotes
- Engrams survive the push→clone→fetch cycle

---

## Phase 6: Review & Graph

**Depends on**: Phase 1, Phase 4

### 6.1 Intent-Based Review (`crates/engram-query/src/review.rs`)

`review_branch(storage, base, head) -> BranchReview` — walks git log for `base..head`, finds commits with `Engram-Id` trailers, collects referenced engrams. Returns `BranchReview` (range, engrams:Vec<ReviewEntry>, total_tokens, total_cost, files_changed).

### 6.2 Context Graph (`crates/engram-query/src/graph/`)

**`model.rs`** — `ContextGraph` (nodes:Vec<GraphNode>, edges:Vec<GraphEdge>). `NodeType` enum (Engram, File, Agent, Commit, Concept). `EdgeType` enum (ModifiedBy, ProducedBy, UsedAgent, FollowsFrom, Motivates, TouchedFile, RejectedIn).

**`builder.rs`** — `build_graph(storage) -> ContextGraph` — iterates all engrams, creates nodes for engrams/agents/files/commits, creates edges from operations and lineage.

**`traversal.rs`** — `subgraph(graph, center_id, depth) -> ContextGraph`, `file_reasoning_chain(graph, file_path) -> Vec<GraphNode>`.

### 6.3 CLI

`Review` command (range e.g. `main..feature`). `Graph` command (node e.g. `file:src/auth.rs`, --depth, --dot for Graphviz output).

### 6.4 Done When

- `engram review main..feature` shows intent chain with cost totals
- `engram graph file:src/auth.rs --depth 2` shows connected entities
- `--dot` output renders in Graphviz

---

## Phase 7: SDKs

**Depends on**: Phase 1

### 7.1 Rust SDK (`crates/engram-sdk/`)

`EngramSession` struct with fluent API matching the readme examples: `begin(agent, model)`, `log_message(role, content)`, `log_tool_call(name, input, output)`, `log_file_change(path, type)`, `log_rejection(approach, reason)`, `add_tokens(input, output, cost)`, `commit(sha, summary) -> EngramId`. Wraps engram-core's GitStorage.

### 7.2 Python SDK (`sdks/python/`)

pyproject.toml with hatchling build, depends on pygit2>=1.14. `EngramSession` class with async context manager matching readme examples. `GitStorage` class using pygit2 for blob/tree/commit/ref creation.

### 7.3 TypeScript SDK (`sdks/typescript/`)

package.json with simple-git dep (shells out to git CLI — more reliable than nodegit). `EngramSession` class matching readme examples. `GitStorage` class using git hash-object/mktree/commit-tree/update-ref commands.

### 7.4 Done When

- All three SDKs produce engrams readable by `engram show`
- Each has tests passing and a usage README

---

## Cross-Cutting Concerns

**Error handling**: thiserror in library crates (typed errors), anyhow in CLI (user-facing context messages).

**Tracing**: `tracing` crate in all libraries. CLI initializes subscriber with env filter (`ENGRAM_LOG=debug` or `-v`/`-vv` flags).

**CI** (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`): Jobs for fmt check, clippy, test (ubuntu+macos+windows), build release, docs.

**Release** (`.github/workflows/release.yml`): On `v*` tags, cross-compile for linux/macos/windows x86_64+aarch64, publish to GitHub Releases and crates.io.

**Versioning**: All workspace crates share version via `workspace.package.version`. Pre-1.0 SemVer: 0.1.0 (Phase 1), 0.2.0 (Phase 2), etc.

---

# Engram: Full Implementation Plan

## Context

Engram is a greenfield Rust project that captures AI agent reasoning (intent, transcripts, tool calls, dead ends, token economics) as native Git objects. The repository currently contains only a design document (`readme`). This plan covers the full build from empty repo to production-ready application across 7 phases.

---

## Phase 1: Foundation (engram-core + engram-cli skeleton)

### 1.1 Cargo Workspace Setup

Create a virtual workspace at the root with two initial crates:

**`/Cargo.toml`** — Virtual manifest:
- `resolver = "2"`, `edition = "2024"`, `rust-version = "1.85"`
- Members: `crates/engram-core`, `crates/engram-cli`
- `[workspace.dependencies]`: git2 0.20, serde 1 (derive), serde_json 1, chrono 0.4 (serde), uuid 1 (v4, serde), thiserror 2, anyhow 1, clap 4.5 (derive, env), tracing 0.1, tracing-subscriber 0.3 (env-filter), tempfile 3, assert_cmd 2, predicates 3

**`crates/engram-core/Cargo.toml`** — Library crate with git2, serde, serde_json, chrono, uuid, thiserror, tracing. Dev-dep: tempfile.

**`crates/engram-cli/Cargo.toml`** — Binary crate (`[[bin]] name = "engram"`), depends on engram-core, clap, anyhow, tracing, tracing-subscriber. Dev-deps: assert_cmd, predicates, tempfile.

Also create: `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (fmt check, clippy, test on ubuntu/macos/windows, build release), `.gitignore`, `LICENSE-MIT`, `LICENSE-APACHE`.

### 1.2 Data Model (`crates/engram-core/src/model/`)

**`engram.rs`** — `EngramId` (newtype around String, UUID v4 hex no dashes), `Manifest` (id, version:u32, created_at, finished_at, agent:AgentInfo, git_commits:Vec<String>, token_usage:TokenUsage, summary:Option<String>, tags:Vec<String>, capture_mode:CaptureMode), `AgentInfo` (name, model:Option, version:Option), `CaptureMode` enum (Wrapper, Import, Sdk). `EngramId::fanout_prefix()` returns first 2 chars.

**`token_economics.rs`** — `TokenUsage` (input_tokens:u64, output_tokens:u64, cache_read_tokens:u64, cache_write_tokens:u64, total_tokens:u64, cost_usd:Option<f64>). Default impl.

**`intent.rs`** — `Intent` (original_request:String, interpreted_goal:Option, summary:Option, dead_ends:Vec<DeadEnd>, decisions:Vec<Decision>), `DeadEnd` (approach, reason), `Decision` (description, rationale). Methods: `to_markdown() -> String`, `from_markdown(&str) -> Result`. Markdown format: `# Intent` / `## Summary` / `## Dead Ends` / `## Decisions` sections.

**`transcript.rs`** — `TranscriptEntry` (timestamp, role:Role, content:TranscriptContent, token_count:Option<u64>), `Role` enum (User, Assistant, System, Tool), `TranscriptContent` internally-tagged enum (Text{text}, ToolUse{tool_name, tool_id, input:Value}, ToolResult{tool_id, output, is_error}, Thinking{text}), `Transcript` (entries:Vec). Methods: `to_jsonl() -> Vec<u8>`, `from_jsonl(&[u8]) -> Result`.

**`operations.rs`** — `Operations` (tool_calls:Vec<ToolCall>, file_changes:Vec<FileChange>, shell_commands:Vec<ShellCommand>), `ToolCall` (timestamp, tool_name, input:Value, output_summary:Option, duration_ms:Option, is_error), `FileChange` (path, change_type:FileChangeType, lines_added:Option, lines_removed:Option), `FileChangeType` enum (Created, Modified, Deleted, Renamed{from}), `ShellCommand` (timestamp, command, exit_code:Option, duration_ms:Option).

**`lineage.rs`** — `Lineage` (parent_engram:Option<EngramId>, child_engrams:Vec, related_engrams:Vec<Relationship>, git_commits:Vec<String>, branch:Option<String>), `Relationship` (engram_id, relation_type:RelationType, description:Option), `RelationType` enum (FollowsFrom, Motivates, DependsOn, Supersedes, ConflictsWith).

**`mod.rs`** — Re-export all public types.

**`EngramData`** aggregate struct (manifest, intent, transcript, operations, lineage) — used for create/read operations.

### 1.3 Git Storage Engine (`crates/engram-core/src/storage/`)

**`objects.rs`** — `create_engram_objects(repo: &Repository, data: &EngramData) -> Result<Oid>`:
1. Serialize each component to bytes (manifest→JSON, intent→Markdown, transcript→JSONL, operations→JSON, lineage→JSON)
2. Create 5 blobs via `repo.blob(&bytes)`
3. Build tree via `repo.treebuilder(None)` → `insert("manifest.json", oid, 0o100644)` for each → `write()`
4. Create commit via `repo.commit(None, &sig, &sig, &message, &tree, &[])` — standalone, no parent
5. Return commit Oid

**`refs.rs`** — Constants: `ENGRAM_REF_PREFIX = "refs/engrams/"`. Functions: `engram_ref_name(id) -> String` (format `refs/engrams/{prefix}/{full}`), `create_engram_ref(repo, id, oid)`, `delete_engram_ref(repo, id)`, `list_engram_refs(repo) -> Vec<(EngramId, Oid)>` (glob `refs/engrams/*/*`).

**`read.rs`** — `read_engram(repo, commit_oid) -> Result<EngramData>` (commit→tree→blobs, deserialize each), `read_manifest(repo, commit_oid) -> Result<Manifest>` (fast path, reads only manifest.json blob). Helpers: `read_blob_bytes`, `read_blob_string`, `read_blob_json<T>`.

**`git_backend.rs`** — `GitStorage` struct wrapping `git2::Repository`. Methods:
- `open(path)`, `discover()` — open/find repo
- `is_initialized() -> bool` — check `engram.enabled` config
- `init()` — set config values, add refspecs to remotes
- `create(data: &EngramData) -> Result<EngramId>` — call objects::create + refs::create
- `read(id) -> Result<EngramData>`, `read_manifest(id) -> Result<Manifest>`
- `list(opts: &ListOptions) -> Result<Vec<Manifest>>` — iterate refs, read manifests
- `delete(id)` — remove ref
- `repo()`, `workdir()` — accessors

### 1.4 Config (`crates/engram-core/src/config/`)

**`settings.rs`** — `EngramConfig` (enabled:bool, auto_capture:bool, default_agent:Option, push_on_push:bool, index_path:Option). Stored in `.git/config` under `[engram]`. Methods: `load(config)`, `save(config)`, `default_init()`.

### 1.5 Error Types (`crates/engram-core/src/error.rs`)

`CoreError` enum with thiserror: Git(git2::Error), NotFound{id}, InvalidManifest(serde_json::Error), NotInitialized, Config(String), Io(io::Error), Utf8(FromUtf8Error), MissingBlob(String).

### 1.6 CLI (`crates/engram-cli/src/`)

**`main.rs`** — Cli struct with clap Parser: `-v` verbosity (count), `--format` (text/json), subcommand. Init tracing subscriber with env filter. Dispatch to command handlers.

**`commands/mod.rs`** — Commands enum: Init, Log, Show, Version.

**`commands/init.rs`** — InitArgs (--force). Opens repo, calls storage.init(), prints next steps.

**`commands/log.rs`** — LogArgs (--cost, -n/--limit, --agent). Lists manifests, formats as table or JSON. Shows: short-id, summary, agent, timestamp, optionally cost/tokens.

**`commands/show.rs`** — ShowArgs (id:String, --intent, --transcript, --operations). Resolves "HEAD" to most recent engram. Displays full engram or requested section.

**`commands/version.rs`** — Prints version from Cargo.toml.

**`output/mod.rs`** — OutputFormat enum (Text, Json). **`output/format.rs`** — Formatting functions for manifests and engram data.

### 1.7 Testing

- **Unit tests**: Serialization roundtrips for all model types. EngramId generation and fanout. Intent markdown roundtrip. Transcript JSONL roundtrip.
- **Storage integration tests** (`crates/engram-core/tests/`): Create temp repo via `git2::Repository::init(tempdir)`, create engram, list, read back, verify all fields, delete, verify gone.
- **CLI integration tests** (`crates/engram-cli/tests/`): `assert_cmd` tests for `engram version`, `engram init` in temp repo, `engram log` (empty).

### 1.8 Done When

- `cargo build --workspace` succeeds with no warnings
- `cargo test --workspace` passes
- `cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings` clean
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` passes
- Full create → list → read → delete lifecycle works

---

## Phase 2: Capture (engram-capture)

**Depends on**: Phase 1

### 2.1 Setup

Add `engram-capture` to workspace. New deps: portable-pty 0.9, vt100 0.15, tokio 1 (full), sha2 0.10.

### 2.2 PTY Wrapper (`crates/engram-capture/src/pty/`)

**`wrapper.rs`** — `PtyWrapperConfig` (command, args, working_dir, agent_name, rows, cols). `PtySession` struct. `PtySession::start(config) -> Result<Self>` snapshots working tree, spawns command in PTY. `PtySession::run(self) -> Result<CapturedSession>` runs to completion, detects file changes.

**`stream.rs`** — `PtyStream` handles bidirectional I/O: stdin→master_writer, master_reader→stdout+capture_buffer. Uses vt100::Parser for ANSI stripping. Runs on threads (not async, because portable-pty I/O is blocking).

**`detector.rs`** — `snapshot_working_tree(root) -> HashMap<PathBuf, Vec<u8>>` (path→SHA256, ignores .git, respects .gitignore). `detect_changes(before, after) -> Vec<FileChange>`.

**`CapturedSession`** struct: raw_output, parsed_screen (cleaned text), start/end time, exit_code, file_changes, command, args.

### 2.3 Session Finalization (`crates/engram-capture/src/session/`)

**`builder.rs`** — `SessionBuilder` takes AgentInfo + CapturedSession, produces EngramData. `build_and_store(storage) -> Result<EngramId>`.

**`summarizer.rs`** — `extract_intent_from_pty(captured) -> Intent` (first arg/line = original_request, file changes = summary). `extract_operations_from_pty(captured) -> Operations` (best-effort for PTY mode).

### 2.4 Git Hooks (`crates/engram-core/src/hooks/`)

**`installer.rs`** — `install_hooks(repo)` writes shell scripts to `.git/hooks/` that invoke `engram hook-handler <hook-name>`. Chains with existing hooks.

**`post_commit.rs`** — Reads `.git/engram-session` (ActiveSession JSON), appends HEAD commit SHA to commits list.

**`prepare_commit_msg.rs`** — Reads active session, appends Engram-Id/Agent/Tokens/Cost trailers to commit message.

**ActiveSession** (stored at `.git/engram-session`): engram_id, agent, started_at, commits:Vec<String>. Created when recording starts, deleted when recording ends.

### 2.5 CLI

Add `Record` command: `engram record -- <command> [args...]`. TrailingVarArg for command. `--agent` override. Lifecycle: create session file → snapshot → spawn PTY → run → detect changes → build engram → store → cleanup → print summary.

### 2.6 Done When

- `engram record -- echo "hello"` captures output and stores engram
- PTY stdin/stdout pass-through works transparently
- File change detection identifies created/modified/deleted files
- Hooks install correctly, trailers added to commits during recording
- `engram log` and `engram show` work with captured engrams

---

## Phase 3: Import (part of engram-capture)

**Depends on**: Phase 1 (Phase 2's session builder is reused but could be factored out)

### 3.1 Claude Code Importer (`crates/engram-capture/src/import/claude_code.rs`)

Parses `~/.claude/projects/<path-encoded>/<sessionId>.jsonl`. Internal types: `ClaudeCodeEntry` (type, parentUuid, uuid, sessionId, message, timestamp), `ClaudeMessage` (role, content:Value, model, usage). Logic:
1. Read JSONL line by line, parse as ClaudeCodeEntry
2. Filter to type "user"/"assistant" (skip "progress", "file-history-snapshot")
3. Build linked list via parentUuid→uuid chains
4. Convert content blocks (text, tool_use, tool_result, thinking) → TranscriptEntry
5. Accumulate TokenUsage from usage fields
6. First user message → Intent.original_request
7. Tool calls → Operations
8. Path encoding: `/Users/sjonas/project` → `-Users-sjonas-project`

Public API: `ClaudeCodeImporter::import_session(path) -> Result<EngramData>`, `discover_sessions(project_path) -> Vec<PathBuf>`, `projects_dir() -> Option<PathBuf>`.

### 3.2 Aider Importer (`crates/engram-capture/src/import/aider.rs`)

Parses `.aider.chat.history.md`. Format: `#### ` = user message, following text = assistant, `> ` = tool output, `Tokens:` lines for costs. Split on `#### ` boundaries, group exchanges into sessions.

### 3.3 Auto-Detection (`crates/engram-capture/src/import/detect.rs`)

`ImportSource` enum (ClaudeCode{path}, Aider{path}). `detect_sources(repo_root) -> Vec<ImportSource>` checks for Claude Code project dir and .aider.chat.history.md.

### 3.4 CLI

Add `Import` command: `engram import [path] --format <fmt> --auto-detect --dry-run`.

### 3.5 Test Fixtures

Create `crates/engram-capture/tests/fixtures/` with sample Claude Code JSONL and Aider markdown files.

### 3.6 Done When

- `engram import <path> --format claude-code` imports correctly
- `engram import --auto-detect` discovers sessions
- Token usage accumulated, tool calls extracted, intent populated

---

## Phase 4: Query & Search (engram-query)

**Depends on**: Phase 1

### 4.1 Setup

Add `engram-query` to workspace. New dep: tantivy 0.25.

### 4.2 Tantivy Schema (`crates/engram-query/src/index/schema.rs`)

`EngramSchema` struct with field handles: id (STRING|STORED), intent_request (TEXT|STORED), intent_summary (TEXT|STORED), transcript_text (TEXT), agent_name (STRING|STORED), agent_model (STRING|STORED), created_at (date INDEXED|STORED), file_paths (TEXT|STORED), dead_ends (TEXT|STORED), cost_usd (f64 INDEXED|STORED), total_tokens (u64 INDEXED|STORED), manifest_json (STORED only).

### 4.3 Writer/Reader

**`index/writer.rs`** — `EngramIndexWriter::open(path)`, `index_engram(data)` (concatenates transcript text entries, dead ends text, file paths into searchable fields), `commit()`, `delete_engram(id)`.

**`index/reader.rs`** — `EngramSearcher::open(path)`, `search(query, limit) -> Vec<SearchResult>` (parses query against intent_request, intent_summary, transcript_text, dead_ends, file_paths fields), `search_by_file(path, limit)`.

**`index/rebuild.rs`** — `rebuild_index(storage, index_path) -> Result<usize>` — deletes and recreates index from all Git engrams.

### 4.4 High-Level APIs

**`search.rs`** — `SearchEngine::open(storage)` (resolves `.git/engram-index/`), delegates to reader.

**`trace.rs`** — `trace_file(storage, search, file_path) -> Vec<TraceEntry>` — all engrams that touched a file.

**`diff.rs`** — `diff_engrams(storage, id_a, id_b) -> EngramDiff` — common files, unique files, token/cost deltas.

### 4.5 CLI

Add commands: `Search` (query, -n/--limit), `Trace` (file path), `Diff` (id_a, id_b), `Reindex`.

Index auto-updates: `GitStorage::create()` checks for `.git/engram-index/` existence and indexes the new engram if present. First `engram search` creates the index if missing.

### 4.6 Done When

- `engram search "auth"` returns relevant results with BM25 ranking
- `engram trace src/auth.rs` shows reasoning history
- `engram reindex` rebuilds from scratch
- Index at `.git/engram-index/` (inside .git, auto-excluded)

---

## Phase 5: Protocol & Sync (engram-protocol)

**Depends on**: Phase 1

### 5.1 Setup

Add `engram-protocol` to workspace. Deps: engram-core, git2, thiserror, tracing.

### 5.2 Implementation

**`refspec.rs`** — Constants: ENGRAM_FETCH_REFSPEC (`+refs/engrams/*:refs/engrams/*`), ENGRAM_PUSH_REFSPEC. `ensure_refspecs(repo, remote_name)` adds if missing.

**`sync.rs`** — `push_engrams(repo, remote, opts) -> PushResult`, `fetch_engrams(repo, remote, opts) -> FetchResult`. Uses `git2::Remote::push/fetch` with engram refspecs. PushOptions: specific_ids, dry_run. FetchOptions: specific_ids, metadata_only.

**`selective.rs`** — Thin engrams (manifest+lineage only) under `refs/engrams-meta/`. `is_full_engram()`, `fetch_full_engram()`.

### 5.3 CLI

Add commands: `Push` (remote, default origin), `Pull` (fetch + reindex), `Fetch` (remote).

### 5.4 Done When

- Push/fetch work between local repos (test with bare repo as remote)
- `engram init` configures refspecs on existing remotes
- Engrams survive the push→clone→fetch cycle

---

## Phase 6: Review & Graph

**Depends on**: Phase 1, Phase 4

### 6.1 Intent-Based Review (`crates/engram-query/src/review.rs`)

`review_branch(storage, base, head) -> BranchReview` — walks git log for `base..head`, finds commits with `Engram-Id` trailers, collects referenced engrams. Returns `BranchReview` (range, engrams:Vec<ReviewEntry>, total_tokens, total_cost, files_changed).

### 6.2 Context Graph (`crates/engram-query/src/graph/`)

**`model.rs`** — `ContextGraph` (nodes:Vec<GraphNode>, edges:Vec<GraphEdge>). `NodeType` enum (Engram, File, Agent, Commit, Concept). `EdgeType` enum (ModifiedBy, ProducedBy, UsedAgent, FollowsFrom, Motivates, TouchedFile, RejectedIn).

**`builder.rs`** — `build_graph(storage) -> ContextGraph` — iterates all engrams, creates nodes for engrams/agents/files/commits, creates edges from operations and lineage.

**`traversal.rs`** — `subgraph(graph, center_id, depth) -> ContextGraph`, `file_reasoning_chain(graph, file_path) -> Vec<GraphNode>`.

### 6.3 CLI

`Review` command (range e.g. `main..feature`). `Graph` command (node e.g. `file:src/auth.rs`, --depth, --dot for Graphviz output).

### 6.4 Done When

- `engram review main..feature` shows intent chain with cost totals
- `engram graph file:src/auth.rs --depth 2` shows connected entities
- `--dot` output renders in Graphviz

---

## Phase 7: SDKs

**Depends on**: Phase 1

### 7.1 Rust SDK (`crates/engram-sdk/`)

`EngramSession` struct with fluent API matching the readme examples: `begin(agent, model)`, `log_message(role, content)`, `log_tool_call(name, input, output)`, `log_file_change(path, type)`, `log_rejection(approach, reason)`, `add_tokens(input, output, cost)`, `commit(sha, summary) -> EngramId`. Wraps engram-core's GitStorage.

### 7.2 Python SDK (`sdks/python/`)

pyproject.toml with hatchling build, depends on pygit2>=1.14. `EngramSession` class with async context manager matching readme examples. `GitStorage` class using pygit2 for blob/tree/commit/ref creation.

### 7.3 TypeScript SDK (`sdks/typescript/`)

package.json with simple-git dep (shells out to git CLI — more reliable than nodegit). `EngramSession` class matching readme examples. `GitStorage` class using git hash-object/mktree/commit-tree/update-ref commands.

### 7.4 Done When

- All three SDKs produce engrams readable by `engram show`
- Each has tests passing and a usage README

---

## Cross-Cutting Concerns

**Error handling**: thiserror in library crates (typed errors), anyhow in CLI (user-facing context messages).

**Tracing**: `tracing` crate in all libraries. CLI initializes subscriber with env filter (`ENGRAM_LOG=debug` or `-v`/`-vv` flags).

**Versioning**: All workspace crates share version via `workspace.package.version`. Pre-1.0 SemVer: 0.1.0 (Phase 1), 0.2.0 (Phase 2), etc.

---

## Verification Plan

After each phase, verify with:

1. `cargo build --workspace && cargo test --workspace && cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings`
2. Manual smoke test of the new CLI commands in a real Git repository

**`refs.rs`** — Constants: `ENGRAM_REF_PREFIX = "refs/engrams/"`. Functions: `engram_ref_name(id) -> String` (format `refs/engrams/{prefix}/{full}`), `create_engram_ref(repo, id, oid)`, `delete_engram_ref(repo, id)`, `list_engram_refs(repo) -> Vec<(EngramId, Oid)>` (glob `refs/engrams/*/*`).

**`read.rs`** — `read_engram(repo, commit_oid) -> Result<EngramData>` (commit→tree→blobs, deserialize each), `read_manifest(repo, commit_oid) -> Result<Manifest>` (fast path, reads only manifest.json blob). Helpers: `read_blob_bytes`, `read_blob_string`, `read_blob_json<T>`.

**`git_backend.rs`** — `GitStorage` struct wrapping `git2::Repository`. Methods:
- `open(path)`, `discover()` — open/find repo
- `is_initialized() -> bool` — check `engram.enabled` config
- `init()` — set config values, add refspecs to remotes
- `create(data: &EngramData) -> Result<EngramId>` — call objects::create + refs::create
- `read(id) -> Result<EngramData>`, `read_manifest(id) -> Result<Manifest>`
- `list(opts: &ListOptions) -> Result<Vec<Manifest>>` — iterate refs, read manifests
- `delete(id)` — remove ref
- `repo()`, `workdir()` — accessors

### 1.4 Config (`crates/engram-core/src/config/`)

**`settings.rs`** — `EngramConfig` (enabled:bool, auto_capture:bool, default_agent:Option, push_on_push:bool, index_path:Option). Stored in `.git/config` under `[engram]`. Methods: `load(config)`, `save(config)`, `default_init()`.

### 1.5 Error Types (`crates/engram-core/src/error.rs`)

`CoreError` enum with thiserror: Git(git2::Error), NotFound{id}, InvalidManifest(serde_json::Error), NotInitialized, Config(String), Io(io::Error), Utf8(FromUtf8Error), MissingBlob(String).

### 1.6 CLI (`crates/engram-cli/src/`)

**`main.rs`** — Cli struct with clap Parser: `-v` verbosity (count), `--format` (text/json), subcommand. Init tracing subscriber with env filter. Dispatch to command handlers.

**`commands/mod.rs`** — Commands enum: Init, Log, Show, Version.

**`commands/init.rs`** — InitArgs (--force). Opens repo, calls storage.init(), prints next steps.

**`commands/log.rs`** — LogArgs (--cost, -n/--limit, --agent). Lists manifests, formats as table or JSON. Shows: short-id, summary, agent, timestamp, optionally cost/tokens.

**`commands/show.rs`** — ShowArgs (id:String, --intent, --transcript, --operations). Resolves "HEAD" to most recent engram. Displays full engram or requested section.

**`commands/version.rs`** — Prints version from Cargo.toml.

**`output/mod.rs`** — OutputFormat enum (Text, Json). **`output/format.rs`** — Formatting functions for manifests and engram data.

### 1.7 Testing

- **Unit tests**: Serialization roundtrips for all model types. EngramId generation and fanout. Intent markdown roundtrip. Transcript JSONL roundtrip.
- **Storage integration tests** (`crates/engram-core/tests/`): Create temp repo via `git2::Repository::init(tempdir)`, create engram, list, read back, verify all fields, delete, verify gone.
- **CLI integration tests** (`crates/engram-cli/tests/`): `assert_cmd` tests for `engram version`, `engram init` in temp repo, `engram log` (empty).

### 1.8 Done When

- `cargo build --workspace` succeeds with no warnings
- `cargo test --workspace` passes
- `cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings` clean
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` passes
- Full create → list → read → delete lifecycle works

## Phase 2: Capture (engram-capture)

**Depends on**: Phase 1

### 2.1 Setup

Add `engram-capture` to workspace. New deps: portable-pty 0.9, vt100 0.15, tokio 1 (full), sha2 0.10.

### 2.2 PTY Wrapper (`crates/engram-capture/src/pty/`)

**`wrapper.rs`** — `PtyWrapperConfig` (command, args, working_dir, agent_name, rows, cols). `PtySession` struct. `PtySession::start(config) -> Result<Self>` snapshots working tree, spawns command in PTY. `PtySession::run(self) -> Result<CapturedSession>` runs to completion, detects file changes.

**`stream.rs`** — `PtyStream` handles bidirectional I/O: stdin→master_writer, master_reader→stdout+capture_buffer. Uses vt100::Parser for ANSI stripping. Runs on threads (not async, because portable-pty I/O is blocking).

**`detector.rs`** — `snapshot_working_tree(root) -> HashMap<PathBuf, Vec<u8>>` (path→SHA256, ignores .git, respects .gitignore). `detect_changes(before, after) -> Vec<FileChange>`.

**`CapturedSession`** struct: raw_output, parsed_screen (cleaned text), start/end time, exit_code, file_changes, command, args.

### 2.3 Session Finalization (`crates/engram-capture/src/session/`)

**`builder.rs`** — `SessionBuilder` takes AgentInfo + CapturedSession, produces EngramData. `build_and_store(storage) -> Result<EngramId>`.

**`summarizer.rs`** — `extract_intent_from_pty(captured) -> Intent` (first arg/line = original_request, file changes = summary). `extract_operations_from_pty(captured) -> Operations` (best-effort for PTY mode).

### 2.4 Git Hooks (`crates/engram-core/src/hooks/`)

**`installer.rs`** — `install_hooks(repo)` writes shell scripts to `.git/hooks/` that invoke `engram hook-handler <hook-name>`. Chains with existing hooks.

**`post_commit.rs`** — Reads `.git/engram-session` (ActiveSession JSON), appends HEAD commit SHA to commits list.

**`prepare_commit_msg.rs`** — Reads active session, appends Engram-Id/Agent/Tokens/Cost trailers to commit message.

**ActiveSession** (stored at `.git/engram-session`): engram_id, agent, started_at, commits:Vec<String>. Created when recording starts, deleted when recording ends.

### 2.5 CLI

Add `Record` command: `engram record -- <command> [args...]`. TrailingVarArg for command. `--agent` override. Lifecycle: create session file → snapshot → spawn PTY → run → detect changes → build engram → store → cleanup → print summary.

### 2.6 Done When

- `engram record -- echo "hello"` captures output and stores engram
- PTY stdin/stdout pass-through works transparently
- File change detection identifies created/modified/deleted files
- Hooks install correctly, trailers added to commits during recording
- `engram log` and `engram show` work with captured engrams

## Phase 3: Import (part of engram-capture)

**Depends on**: Phase 1 (Phase 2's session builder is reused but could be factored out)

### 3.1 Claude Code Importer (`crates/engram-capture/src/import/claude_code.rs`)

Parses `~/.claude/projects/<path-encoded>/<sessionId>.jsonl`. Internal types: `ClaudeCodeEntry` (type, parentUuid, uuid, sessionId, message, timestamp), `ClaudeMessage` (role, content:Value, model, usage). Logic:
1. Read JSONL line by line, parse as ClaudeCodeEntry
2. Filter to type "user"/"assistant" (skip "progress", "file-history-snapshot")
3. Build linked list via parentUuid→uuid chains
4. Convert content blocks (text, tool_use, tool_result, thinking) → TranscriptEntry
5. Accumulate TokenUsage from usage fields
6. First user message → Intent.original_request
7. Tool calls → Operations
8. Path encoding: `/Users/sjonas/project` → `-Users-sjonas-project`

Public API: `ClaudeCodeImporter::import_session(path) -> Result<EngramData>`, `discover_sessions(project_path) -> Vec<PathBuf>`, `projects_dir() -> Option<PathBuf>`.

### 3.2 Aider Importer (`crates/engram-capture/src/import/aider.rs`)

Parses `.aider.chat.history.md`. Format: `#### ` = user message, following text = assistant, `> ` = tool output, `Tokens:` lines for costs. Split on `#### ` boundaries, group exchanges into sessions.

### 3.3 Auto-Detection (`crates/engram-capture/src/import/detect.rs`)

`ImportSource` enum (ClaudeCode{path}, Aider{path}). `detect_sources(repo_root) -> Vec<ImportSource>` checks for Claude Code project dir and .aider.chat.history.md.

### 3.4 CLI

Add `Import` command: `engram import [path] --format <fmt> --auto-detect --dry-run`.

### 3.5 Test Fixtures

Create `crates/engram-capture/tests/fixtures/` with sample Claude Code JSONL and Aider markdown files.

### 3.6 Done When

- `engram import <path> --format claude-code` imports correctly
- `engram import --auto-detect` discovers sessions
- Token usage accumulated, tool calls extracted, intent populated

## Phase 4: Query & Search (engram-query)

**Depends on**: Phase 1

### 4.1 Setup

Add `engram-query` to workspace. New dep: tantivy 0.25.

### 4.2 Tantivy Schema (`crates/engram-query/src/index/schema.rs`)

`EngramSchema` struct with field handles: id (STRING|STORED), intent_request (TEXT|STORED), intent_summary (TEXT|STORED), transcript_text (TEXT), agent_name (STRING|STORED), agent_model (STRING|STORED), created_at (date INDEXED|STORED), file_paths (TEXT|STORED), dead_ends (TEXT|STORED), cost_usd (f64 INDEXED|STORED), total_tokens (u64 INDEXED|STORED), manifest_json (STORED only).

### 4.3 Writer/Reader

**`index/writer.rs`** — `EngramIndexWriter::open(path)`, `index_engram(data)` (concatenates transcript text entries, dead ends text, file paths into searchable fields), `commit()`, `delete_engram(id)`.

**`index/reader.rs`** — `EngramSearcher::open(path)`, `search(query, limit) -> Vec<SearchResult>` (parses query against intent_request, intent_summary, transcript_text, dead_ends, file_paths fields), `search_by_file(path, limit)`.

**`index/rebuild.rs`** — `rebuild_index(storage, index_path) -> Result<usize>` — deletes and recreates index from all Git engrams.

### 4.4 High-Level APIs

**`search.rs`** — `SearchEngine::open(storage)` (resolves `.git/engram-index/`), delegates to reader.

**`trace.rs`** — `trace_file(storage, search, file_path) -> Vec<TraceEntry>` — all engrams that touched a file.

**`diff.rs`** — `diff_engrams(storage, id_a, id_b) -> EngramDiff` — common files, unique files, token/cost deltas.

### 4.5 CLI

Add commands: `Search` (query, -n/--limit), `Trace` (file path), `Diff` (id_a, id_b), `Reindex`.

Index auto-updates: `GitStorage::create()` checks for `.git/engram-index/` existence and indexes the new engram if present. First `engram search` creates the index if missing.

### 4.6 Done When

- `engram search "auth"` returns relevant results with BM25 ranking
- `engram trace src/auth.rs` shows reasoning history
- `engram reindex` rebuilds from scratch
- Index at `.git/engram-index/` (inside .git, auto-excluded)

## Phase 5: Protocol & Sync (engram-protocol)

**Depends on**: Phase 1

### 5.1 Setup

Add `engram-protocol` to workspace. Deps: engram-core, git2, thiserror, tracing.

### 5.2 Implementation

**`refspec.rs`** — Constants: ENGRAM_FETCH_REFSPEC (`+refs/engrams/*:refs/engrams/*`), ENGRAM_PUSH_REFSPEC. `ensure_refspecs(repo, remote_name)` adds if missing.

**`sync.rs`** — `push_engrams(repo, remote, opts) -> PushResult`, `fetch_engrams(repo, remote, opts) -> FetchResult`. Uses `git2::Remote::push/fetch` with engram refspecs. PushOptions: specific_ids, dry_run. FetchOptions: specific_ids, metadata_only.

**`selective.rs`** — Thin engrams (manifest+lineage only) under `refs/engrams-meta/`. `is_full_engram()`, `fetch_full_engram()`.

### 5.3 CLI

Add commands: `Push` (remote, default origin), `Pull` (fetch + reindex), `Fetch` (remote).

## Phase 6: Review & Graph

**Depends on**: Phase 1, Phase 4

### 6.1 Intent-Based Review (`crates/engram-query/src/review.rs`)

`review_branch(storage, base, head) -> BranchReview` — walks git log for `base..head`, finds commits with `Engram-Id` trailers, collects referenced engrams. Returns `BranchReview` (range, engrams:Vec<ReviewEntry>, total_tokens, total_cost, files_changed).

### 6.2 Context Graph (`crates/engram-query/src/graph/`)

**`model.rs`** — `ContextGraph` (nodes:Vec<GraphNode>, edges:Vec<GraphEdge>). `NodeType` enum (Engram, File, Agent, Commit, Concept). `EdgeType` enum (ModifiedBy, ProducedBy, UsedAgent, FollowsFrom, Motivates, TouchedFile, RejectedIn).

**`builder.rs`** — `build_graph(storage) -> ContextGraph` — iterates all engrams, creates nodes for engrams/agents/files/commits, creates edges from operations and lineage.

**`traversal.rs`** — `subgraph(graph, center_id, depth) -> ContextGraph`, `file_reasoning_chain(graph, file_path) -> Vec<GraphNode>`.

### 6.3 CLI

`Review` command (range e.g. `main..feature`). `Graph` command (node e.g. `file:src/auth.rs`, --depth, --dot for Graphviz output).

## Phase 7: SDKs

**Depends on**: Phase 1

### 7.1 Rust SDK (`crates/engram-sdk/`)

`EngramSession` struct with fluent API matching the readme examples: `begin(agent, model)`, `log_message(role, content)`, `log_tool_call(name, input, output)`, `log_file_change(path, type)`, `log_rejection(approach, reason)`, `add_tokens(input, output, cost)`, `commit(sha, summary) -> EngramId`. Wraps engram-core's GitStorage.

### 7.2 Python SDK (`sdks/python/`)

pyproject.toml with hatchling build, depends on pygit2>=1.14. `EngramSession` class with async context manager matching readme examples. `GitStorage` class using pygit2 for blob/tree/commit/ref creation.

### 7.3 TypeScript SDK (`sdks/typescript/`)

package.json with simple-git dep (shells out to git CLI — more reliable than nodegit). `EngramSession` class matching readme examples. `GitStorage` class using git hash-object/mktree/commit-tree/update-ref commands.

### 7.4 Done When

- All three SDKs produce engrams readable by `engram show`

## Cross-Cutting Concerns

**Error handling**: thiserror in library crates (typed errors), anyhow in CLI (user-facing context messages).

**Tracing**: `tracing` crate in all libraries. CLI initializes subscriber with env filter (`ENGRAM_LOG=debug` or `-v`/`-vv` flags).

**CI** (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`): Jobs for fmt check, clippy, test (ubuntu+macos+windows), build release, docs.

**Release** (`.github/workflows/release.yml`): On `v*` tags, cross-compile for linux/macos/windows x86_64+aarch64, publish to GitHub Releases and crates.io.

**Versioning**: All workspace crates share version via `workspace.package.version`. Pre-1.0 SemVer: 0.1.0 (Phase 1), 0.2.0 (Phase 2), etc.

---

After each phase, verify with:

1. `cargo build --workspace && cargo test --workspace && cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings`
2. Manual smoke test of the new CLI commands in a real Git repository

6. For Phase 4: `engram search "test" && engram reindex`
7. For Phase 5: Create bare remote, `engram push`, clone, verify engrams present
8. For Phase 6: `engram review HEAD~3..HEAD` on a repo with engrams
9. For Phase 7: Run each SDK's test suite

# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

## Project Overview

Engram captures AI agent reasoning as first-class, versioned data in Git. Each "engram" is a discrete unit of reasoning memory (intent, transcript, tool calls, rejected approaches, token economics) linked to the Git commits it produced. Engrams are stored as native Git objects under `.git/refs/engrams/` — no sidecar database.

## Build Commands

```bash
source "$HOME/.cargo/env"             # Ensure cargo is on PATH
cargo build --workspace               # Build all crates
cargo test --workspace                # Run all tests (24 currently)
cargo test -p engram-core             # Test a single crate
cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings  # Lint
cargo fmt --all -- --check            # Format check
cargo run -p engram-cli -- <cmd>      # Run the CLI (e.g., init, log, show, version)
```

## Architecture

Cargo workspace with crates under `crates/`:

```
crates/engram-core/    Core library: data model, Git storage engine, config, error types
crates/engram-cli/     CLI binary (installed as `engram`)
```

Future crates (not yet implemented): `engram-capture`, `engram-query`, `engram-protocol`, `engram-sdk`, plus `sdks/python/` and `sdks/typescript/`.

### engram-core structure

- `src/model/` — Data types: `EngramId`, `Manifest`, `AgentInfo`, `TokenUsage`, `Intent`, `Transcript`, `TranscriptEntry`, `Operations`, `Lineage`, `EngramData` (aggregate)
- `src/storage/` — Git storage engine:
  - `git_backend.rs` — `GitStorage` struct: main CRUD facade (create/read/list/delete engrams)
  - `objects.rs` — Creates Git blobs, trees, and commits for an engram
  - `refs.rs` — Manages refs under `refs/engrams/<ab>/<full-id>` with fanout
  - `read.rs` — Reads engram data back from Git objects
- `src/config/` — `EngramConfig` stored in `.git/config` under `[engram]`
- `src/error.rs` — `CoreError` enum (thiserror)
- `src/hooks/` — Placeholder for git hook handlers (Phase 2)

### engram-cli structure

- `src/main.rs` — clap-based CLI with subcommands and tracing init
- `src/commands/` — `init`, `log`, `show`, `version`
- `src/output/` — `OutputFormat` (text/json) and formatting functions

## Key Design Decisions

- **Git object model**: ref → commit → tree → 5 blobs (manifest.json, intent.md, transcript.jsonl, operations.json, lineage.json)
- **EngramId**: UUID v4 hex (no dashes, 32 chars). Fanout via first 2 chars in ref path.
- **git2 crate** (v0.20, vendored) for all Git operations — TreeBuilder, blob(), commit(), reference()
- **Error strategy**: `thiserror` in libraries, `anyhow` in CLI
- **Tracing**: `tracing` crate, controlled via `-v` flags or `ENGRAM_LOG` env var

## License

Apache-2.0 OR MIT (dual-licensed).

content.text: One test failure in the Aider importer. Let me check the test and fix it.
The test expects `input_tokens` to be 4700 (3200 + 1500), but the actual result is 7000. Let me look at how tokens are parsed and accumulated.

The issue is in the `parse_token_line` function. It splits on `[',', '.']`. Let's trace through:

Input line 1: `"Tokens: 3.2k sent, 245 received. Cost: $0.01"`

Splitting on `,` and `.`:
1. `"Tokens: 3"` — contains neither "sent", "received", nor "$"
2. `"2k sent"` — contains "sent", extract_token_count("2k sent") = 2000
3. `" 245 received"` — contains "received", extract_token_count = 245


4. `" Cost: $0"` — contains "$", extract_cost("Cost: $0") = Some(0.0)
5. `"01"` — no match

The problem is that splitting on `.` breaks up decimal numbers like `3.2k` and `$0.01`. I need to change the approach—either split only on commas and handle the cost section separately, or use a more intelligent parsing strategy that respects decimal points.

Looking at the actual format `"Tokens: 3.2k sent, 245 received. Cost: $0.01"`, the periods are causing issues. A better approach is to split on commas first, then check each segment for "sent", "received", or cost indicators like "$". Let me refactor `parse_token_line` to handle this correctly.
I see the bug. `parse_token_line` splits on `[',', '.']` which breaks up `3.2k` into `3` and `2k`, and `$0.01` into `$0` and `01`. It should only split on `,` and handle `.` differently.

# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

## Project Overview

Engram captures AI agent reasoning as first-class, versioned data in Git. Each "engram" is a discrete unit of reasoning memory (intent, transcript, tool calls, rejected approaches, token economics) linked to the Git commits it produced. Engrams are stored as native Git objects under `.git/refs/engrams/` — no sidecar database.

## Build Commands

```bash
source "$HOME/.cargo/env"             # Ensure cargo is on PATH
cargo build --workspace               # Build all crates
cargo test --workspace                # Run all tests (39 currently)
cargo test -p engram-core             # Test a single crate
cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings  # Lint
cargo fmt --all -- --check            # Format check
cargo run -p engram-cli -- <cmd>      # Run the CLI
```

## Architecture

Cargo workspace with 6 crates under `crates/`:

```
crates/engram-core/      Core library: data model, Git storage engine, config, error types
crates/engram-capture/   PTY wrapper, file change detection, session builder, importers (Claude Code, Aider)
crates/engram-query/     Tantivy full-text search index, file tracing, engram diff, context graph, branch review
crates/engram-protocol/  Push/pull/fetch engram refs between repos via Git refspecs
crates/engram-sdk/       Fluent Rust SDK: EngramSession::begin() → log_*() → commit()
crates/engram-cli/       CLI binary (installed as `engram`) — 15 subcommands
```

### CLI Commands

`init`, `record`, `import`, `log`, `show`, `search`, `trace`, `diff`, `graph`, `review`, `push`, `pull`, `fetch`, `reindex`, `version`

### engram-core structure

- `src/model/` — Data types: `EngramId`, `Manifest`, `AgentInfo`, `TokenUsage`, `Intent`, `Transcript`, `Operations`, `Lineage`, `EngramData`
- `src/storage/` — Git storage engine:
  - `git_backend.rs` — `GitStorage`: main CRUD facade (discover/open/create/read/list/delete)
  - `objects.rs` — Creates Git blobs, trees, and commits for an engram
  - `refs.rs` — Manages refs under `refs/engrams/<ab>/<full-id>` with fanout
  - `read.rs` — Reads engram data back from Git objects
- `src/config/` — `EngramConfig` in `.git/config` under `[engram]`
- `src/error.rs` — `CoreError` enum (thiserror)

### engram-capture structure

- `src/pty/` — PTY wrapper (portable-pty), file change detector (SHA256 snapshots via walkdir+sha2)
- `src/session/` — SessionBuilder: CapturedSession → EngramData
- `src/import/` — Claude Code JSONL parser, Aider markdown parser, auto-detection

### engram-query structure

- `src/index/` — Tantivy schema, writer, reader, rebuild
- `src/search.rs` — High-level SearchEngine with auto-index lifecycle
- `src/trace.rs` — File reasoning trace
- `src/diff.rs` — Compare two engrams (files, tokens, cost)
- `src/graph/` — Context graph (nodes: engram/file/agent/commit; DOT output)
- `src/review.rs` — Branch review: walks git log for Engram-Id trailers

## Key Design Decisions

- **Git object model**: ref → commit → tree → 5 blobs (manifest.json, intent.md, transcript.jsonl, operations.json, lineage.json)
- **EngramId**: UUID v4 hex (no dashes, 32 chars). Fanout via first 2 chars in ref path.

input.content:
# Engram

**Capture agent reasoning as first-class, versioned data in Git.**

Git commits capture *what* changed but discard *why*. When AI agents code, the reasoning trail -- 100K+ tokens of explored alternatives, architectural tradeoffs, rejected approaches -- IS the institutional knowledge. Engram makes reasoning first-class, versioned, and queryable, stored in Git itself.

Each **engram** is a discrete unit of reasoning memory: the full session transcript, human intent, agent decisions, tool calls, dead ends explored, and token economics -- linked to the Git commits it produced.

## Quick Start

```bash
# Build from source
cargo install --path crates/engram-cli

# Initialize in your repo
engram init

# Record an agent session (wraps any agent command in a PTY)
engram record -- claude "add OAuth2 authentication"

# Import existing sessions from Claude Code or Aider
engram import --auto-detect

# Explore reasoning history
engram log --cost
engram show HEAD --intent
engram search "authentication"
engram trace src/auth.rs

# Review by intent, not by diff
engram review main..feature-branch

# Push reasoning alongside code
engram push
```

## Why Engram?

**Without Engram**, your Git history looks like:
```
abc123 Add OAuth2 with PKCE flow
def456 Fix middleware ordering bug
789abc Refactor auth to use sessions
```

**With Engram**, every commit carries its reasoning:
```
abc123 Add OAuth2 with PKCE flow [claude-code/claude-sonnet-4-5] $0.23 47832tok
  Intent: "Add OAuth2 authentication with PKCE for our SPA"
  Summary: Implemented OAuth2 with PKCE using custom middleware. Added
           token refresh, CSRF protection, and session management.
  Dead ends: Tried passport.js (middleware conflict), considered Auth0
             SDK (added 2MB to bundle, decided against).
  Files: +src/auth.rs +src/middleware/oauth.rs ~src/routes/api.rs

def456 Fix middleware ordering bug
  Intent: "The auth middleware runs after the rate limiter, causing 401s"
  Summary: Reordered middleware stack. Auth must run before rate limiting.
  Related: Follows from abc123 (the original auth implementation)
```

This is **institutional knowledge** that compounds. When the next agent (or human) touches auth, they see the full reasoning chain -- what was tried, what was rejected, and why.

## Three Capture Modes

### Mode 1: Wrapper (any agent)
```bash
engram record -- claude "add auth"
engram record -- aider --model gpt-4o
engram record -- cursor-cli "fix the bug"
```
Spawns your agent in a PTY, captures output, detects file changes via SHA256 snapshots.

### Mode 2: Session Import
```bash
engram import --auto-detect                              # Find and import from known agents
engram import ~/.claude/projects/.../session.jsonl --format claude-code
engram import .aider.chat.history.md --format aider
engram import --dry-run                                  # Preview what would be imported
```
Parses Claude Code JSONL sessions and Aider chat history markdown. Extracts transcripts, tool calls, token usage, and file changes.

### Mode 3: SDK Integration

**Rust:**
```rust
use engram_sdk::EngramSession;

let mut session = EngramSession::begin("my-agent", Some("claude-sonnet-4-5"));
session.log_message("user", "Add OAuth2 authentication");
session.log_message("assistant", "Implementing OAuth2 with PKCE...");
session.log_tool_call("write_file", r#"{"path":"src/auth.rs"}"#, Some("Created auth module"));
session.log_file_change("src/auth.rs", "created");
session.log_rejection("passport.js", "Middleware conflict with existing stack");
session.add_tokens(1500, 800, Some(0.02));
let id = session.commit(Some("abc123"), Some("Implemented OAuth2 with PKCE")).unwrap();
```

## Git-Native Storage

Engrams are stored as native Git objects -- they travel with `clone`, `push`, `pull`. No sidecar database, no separate sync, no vendor lock-in.

```
.git/refs/engrams/
  ab/
    abc123...  -> commit -> tree containing:
      manifest.json        # Compact metadata for fast listing
      intent.md            # Human-readable reasoning summary
      transcript.jsonl     # Full session, one message per line
      operations.json      # Tool calls, file ops, shell commands
      lineage.json         # Relationships to other engrams
```

Engrams sync alongside code:
```bash
engram push              # Push engram refs to remote
engram pull              # Fetch engram refs and reindex
engram fetch             # Fetch only (no reindex)
```

## Search and Query

Full-text search powered by Tantivy, stored at `.git/engram-index/`:

```bash
# Search across intent, transcript, file paths, dead ends
engram search "authentication"
engram search "database migration" -n 20

# Trace the full reasoning history of a file
engram trace src/auth.rs

# Compare two engrams (files, tokens, cost)
engram diff abc123 def456

# Rebuild search index from scratch
engram reindex
```

## Context Graph

Engrams form a **context graph** -- a semantic reasoning layer over your codebase:

```bash
# Explore connections between engrams, files, and agents
engram graph
engram graph file:src/auth.rs --depth 2

# Export as Graphviz DOT format
engram graph --dot | dot -Tsvg -o graph.svg
```

Nodes are engrams, files, agents, and commits. Edges are "modified by", "used agent", "follows from", "touched file", "produced by".

## Intent-Based Review

```bash
engram review main..feature-branch
```

Instead of line-by-line code review, read the chain of intents and summaries. See what was asked, what was done, what dead ends were explored, and what architectural decisions were made. Includes aggregate token usage and cost.

## CLI Reference

| Command    | Description |
|------------|-------------|
| `init`     | Initialize engram in a Git repository |
| `record`   | Record an agent session via PTY wrapper |
| `import`   | Import sessions from Claude Code or Aider |
| `log`      | List engrams (most recent first) |
| `show`     | Show details of a specific engram |
| `search`   | Full-text search across engrams |
| `trace`    | Show reasoning history for a file |
| `diff`     | Compare two engrams |
| `graph`    | Show the context graph (text or DOT) |
| `review`   | Review intent chain for a branch range |
| `push`     | Push engram refs to a remote |
| `pull`     | Pull engram refs and reindex |
| `fetch`    | Fetch engram refs from a remote |
| `reindex`  | Rebuild the search index |
| `version`  | Print version information |

All commands support `--format json` for machine-readable output and `-v`/`-vv`/`-vvv` for verbosity.

## Architecture

```
crates/
  engram-core/       Data model, Git storage engine, config
  engram-capture/    PTY wrapper, file change detection, session importers
  engram-query/      Tantivy search index, context graph, branch review
  engram-protocol/   Push/pull/fetch via Git refspecs
  engram-sdk/        Fluent Rust SDK for direct agent integration
  engram-cli/        CLI binary (installed as `engram`)
```

### Design Principles

- **Git-native**: Engrams are Git objects (blobs, trees, commits, refs). No external database.
- **Zero config remotes**: Engram refs sync with standard `git push`/`fetch` via refspecs.
- **Vendored dependencies**: git2 with vendored libgit2 + OpenSSL. No system deps beyond a C compiler.
- **No unsafe code**: `unsafe_code = "forbid"` workspace-wide.
- **Library-first**: All functionality lives in library crates; the CLI is a thin wrapper.

## Building from Source

```bash
# Clone and build
git clone https://github.com/your-org/engram.git
cd engram
cargo build --workspace

# Run tests
cargo test --workspace

# Install the CLI
cargo install --path crates/engram-cli
```

Requires Rust 1.80+ and a C compiler (for vendored libgit2/OpenSSL).

## License

Apache-2.0 OR MIT

1→# Engram
     2→
     3→**Capture agent reasoning as first-class, versioned data in Git.**
     4→
     5→Git commits are lossy. They capture *what* changed but discard *why*. When AI agents code, the reasoning trail — 100K+ tokens of explored alternatives, architectural tradeoffs, rejected approaches — IS the institutional knowledge. Engram makes reasoning first-class, versioned, and queryable, stored in Git itself.
     6→
     7→Each **engram** is a discrete unit of reasoning memory: the full session transcript, human intent, agent decisions, tool calls, dead ends explored, and token economics — linked to the Git commits it produced.
     8→
     9→## Quick Start
    10→
    11→```bash
    12→# Install
    13→cargo install engram
    14→
    15→# Initialize in your repo
    16→engram init
    17→
    18→# Record an agent session (wraps any agent command)
    19→engram record -- claude "add OAuth2 authentication"
    20→

    22→git commit -am "Add OAuth2 with PKCE flow"
    23→

    30→# Review by intent, not by diff
    31→engram review main..feature-branch
    32→
    33→# Push reasoning alongside code
    34→engram push
    35→```
    36→
    37→## Why Engram?
    38→
    39→**Without Engram**, your Git history looks like:
    40→```
    41→abc123 Add OAuth2 with PKCE flow
    42→def456 Fix middleware ordering bug
    43→789abc Refactor auth to use sessions
    44→```
    45→
    46→**With Engram**, every commit carries its reasoning:
    47→```
    48→◆ abc123 Add OAuth2 with PKCE flow [claude-code/claude-sonnet-4-5] $0.23 47832tok
    49→  Intent: "Add OAuth2 authentication with PKCE for our SPA"
    50→  Summary: Implemented OAuth2 with PKCE using custom middleware. Added
    51→           token refresh, CSRF protection, and session management.
    52→  Dead ends: Tried passport.js (middleware conflict), considered Auth0
    53→             SDK (added 2MB to bundle, decided against).
    54→  Files: +src/auth.rs +src/middleware/oauth.rs ~src/routes/api.rs
    55→
    56→○ def456 Fix middleware ordering bug
    57→  Intent: "The auth middleware runs after the rate limiter, causing 401s"
    58→  Summary: Reordered middleware stack. Auth must run before rate limiting.
    59→  Related: Follows from abc123 (the original auth implementation)
    60→```
    61→
    62→This is **institutional knowledge** that compounds. When the next agent (or human) touches auth, they see the full reasoning chain — what was tried, what was rejected, and why.
    63→
    64→## Three Capture Modes
    65→
    66→### Mode 1: Wrapper (works today, any agent)
    67→```bash
    68→engram record -- claude "add auth"
    69→engram record -- aider --model gpt-4o
    70→engram record -- cursor-cli "fix the bug"
    71→```
    72→Spawns your agent in a PTY, captures everything, detects file changes.
    73→
    74→### Mode 2: Session Import
    75→```bash
    76→engram import --auto-detect         # Find and import from known agents
    77→engram import ~/.claude/sessions/latest/ --format claude-code
    78→engram import .aider.chat.history.md --format aider
    79→```
    80→
    81→### Mode 3: SDK Integration (target state)
    82→
    83→**Python:**
    84→```python
    85→from engram import EngramSession
    86→
    87→async with EngramSession("my-agent", "claude-sonnet-4-5") as session:
    88→    session.log_message("user", "Add OAuth2 authentication")
    89→    session.log_message("assistant", "Implementing OAuth2 with PKCE...")
    90→    session.log_tool_call("write_file", {"path": "src/auth.rs"})
    91→    session.log_file_change("src/auth.rs", "created")
    92→    session.log_rejection("passport.js", "Middleware conflict with existing stack")
    93→
    94→    result = await session.commit("abc123", summary="Implemented OAuth2 with PKCE")
    95→```
    96→
    97→**TypeScript:**
    98→```typescript
    99→import { EngramSession } from '@engram/sdk';
   100→
   101→const session = await EngramSession.begin('my-agent', 'claude-sonnet-4-5');
   102→await session.logMessage('user', 'Add OAuth2 authentication');
   103→await session.logToolCall('write_file', { path: 'src/auth.rs' });
   104→session.logRejection('passport.js', 'Middleware conflict');
   105→const result = await session.commit('abc123', { summary: 'Implemented OAuth2 with PKCE' });
   106→```
   107→
   108→**Rust:**
   109→```rust
   110→use engram_sdk::EngramSession;
   111→
   112→let mut session = EngramSession::begin("my-agent", "claude-sonnet-4-5").await?;
   113→session.log_message("user", "Add OAuth2 authentication").await?;
   114→session.log_tool_call("write_file", json!({"path": "auth.rs"}), None).await?;
   115→session.log_rejection("passport.js", "Middleware conflict");
   116→session.commit("abc123", Some("Implemented OAuth2 with PKCE"), None).await?;
   117→```
   118→
   119→## Git-Native Storage
   120→
   121→Engrams are stored as native Git objects — they travel with `clone`, `push`, `pull`. No sidecar database, no separate sync, no vendor lock-in.
   122→
   123→```
   124→.git/refs/engrams/
   125→  ab/
   126→    abc123...  → tree object containing:
   127→      ├── manifest.json        # Compact metadata for fast listing
   128→      ├── intent.md            # Human-readable reasoning summary
   129→      ├── transcript.jsonl     # Full session, one message per line
   130→      ├── operations.json      # Tool calls, file ops, shell commands
   131→      └── lineage.json         # Relationships to other engrams
   132→```
   133→
   134→Commit messages get trailers for discoverability:
   135→```
   136→Add OAuth2 with PKCE flow
   137→
   138→Engram-Id: a3f8c2d...
   139→Engram-Agent: claude-code/claude-sonnet-4-5
   140→Engram-Tokens: 47832
   141→Engram-Cost: $0.23
   142→```
   143→
   144→## The Context Graph
   145→
   146→Engrams form a growing **context graph** — a semantic reasoning layer over your codebase:
   147→
   148→```bash
   149→# Trace the full reasoning history of a file
   150→engram trace src/auth.rs
   151→
   152→# Explore connections between engrams, files, and agents
   153→engram graph file:src/auth.rs --depth 2
   154→
   155→# See which agent sessions touched overlapping files
   156→engram diff abc123 def456
   157→```
   158→
   159→Nodes are engrams, files, functions, agents, and concepts. Edges are "modified by", "motivated by", "depends on", "rejected in favor of". This is the foundation for multi-agent coordination — agents read each other's engrams before starting work.
   160→
   161→## Intent-Based Review
   162→
   163→```bash
   164→engram review main..feature-branch
   165→```
   166→
   167→Instead of line-by-line code review, read the chain of intents and summaries. See what was asked, what was done, what dead ends were explored, and what architectural decisions were made. Code becomes evidence that intent was fulfilled.
   168→
   169→## Architecture
   170→
   171→```
   172→engram-cli          CLI binary — the user interface
   173→engram-core         Data model, Git storage engine, hooks, config
   174→engram-capture      Session capture (wrapper, import, HTTP server)
   175→engram-query        Search index (Tantivy), context graph, analytics
   176→engram-protocol     Wire format for agent ↔ server communication
   177→engram-sdk          Rust SDK for direct agent integration
   178→sdks/python/        Python SDK
   179→sdks/typescript/    TypeScript SDK
   180→```
   181→
   182→## The Strategic Bet
   183→
   184→Code is commodity output. Intent, reasoning, and coordination metadata is where value accumulates. Engram seeds that data layer in every repo.
   185→
   186→Whoever captures the reasoning layer of AI-assisted development owns the developer graph for the next decade.
